featured.title: Capricornus
featured.sunPasses: The Sun is actually in this constellation from about Jan 20 to Feb 15
featured.myth: Half goat, half fish. Mesopotamian sky-watchers saw Enki's goat-fish; the Greeks linked it to Pan, who dived into the Nile and grew a fish's tail.
featured.fact: A faint, wide crescent rather than a bright shape, so it rewards a dark sky and a patient eye. It holds the globular cluster M30.

stars.name: Deneb Algedi
stars.note: Brightest star here; the name means 'the kid's tail'

stars.name: Dabih
stars.note: A bright double for sharp eyes

stars.name: Algedi
stars.note: 'The kid'; a wide pair with α¹ Cap

featured.title: Sagittarius
featured.sunPasses: The Sun is actually in this constellation from about Dec 18 to Jan 18
featured.myth: A centaur drawing his bow, with the arrow aimed at the heart of Scorpius. The brightest stars form the famous 'Teapot'.
featured.fact: Look this way and you look toward the centre of our galaxy, about 26,000 light-years away, rich in star clouds and glowing nebulae.

stars.name: Kaus Australis
stars.note: Brightest star in the Archer; 'southern part of the bow'

stars.name: Nunki
stars.note: Blue-white and hot; the Teapot's handle star

stars.name: Ascella
stars.note: 'The armpit' of the archer; a close pair

stars.name: Kaus Media
stars.note: The middle of the bow, an orange giant

stars.name: Alnasl
stars.note: The arrow's tip, the Teapot's spout
